name: pending_transactions
description: A cross-community transfer while it is still in flight. Both communities hold a row; it becomes a transactions row when the transfer settles, and is dropped when it reverts.

columns.name: state
columns.description: NEW, PENDING, SETTLED or REVERTED — the four steps of server/federation/send-coins.json.

columns.name: pending_transactions_previous_key
columns.description: The preceding transaction of the same account. Unique, exactly as on transactions: no two rows may claim the same predecessor.

columns.name: balance_gdd4
columns.description: Account balance this transfer would leave behind, at balance_date.

columns.name: linked_user_id
columns.description: NULL when the other side is a member of the other community and unknown here.

columns.name: linked_user_gradido_id
columns.note: The entity says nullable, migration 0071 created the column NOT NULL. The database is the stricter one; written here as the entity has it because that is what the code assumes. Confirm against the live schema before generating DDL.

notes: This table mirrors transactions column for column, minus the append-only rule. That is deliberate: settling means moving the row's content into transactions unchanged, so any column that exists on one and not the other is a settle-time conversion waiting to go wrong.

Rows are short-lived. Both communities delete or settle them; a row that stays PENDING past FEDERATION_AUTHENTICATION_TIMEOUT_MS is a stuck transfer, and both implementations must decide it the same way rather than leaving it to whoever notices.
Unlike transactions, this table has no index at all in legacy — not even on user_id — although the balance calculation reads it per user. Whatever gradido2 reads it by belongs in this file.
The denormalized name and uuid columns raise the same footprint question transactions.json records as open. Answer it once, for both.
Timestamps are UTC milliseconds; see types/Timestamp.json. This table uses datetime(3) throughout.
